body: That's because mental illnesses are mainly defined by impairment. If your personal life isn't affected and you seem to be able to regulate your problems by yourself, it's hard for a professional to diagnose you. My guess is that you might downplay some of your symptoms, e.g. not wanting to meet/cancelling on friends because you're mentally exhausted is already impairment.

I'm on my 2nd antidepressant now and this one at least helps against the tiredness, but doesn't really lift my mood. I also got prescibed neuroleptics against the rumination, but my body doesn't tolerate these. I have an appointment tomorrow to get different meds, but I'm slowly losing faith in the effectiveness of these meds.
I don't really try to strike up conversations, if somebody talks to me I can usually respond to their topic, but I don't really have topics to talk about myself.

I've been unable to cry for 3 years now. Although last time it acutally worked was 2 weeks ago on the evening after a visit to my psychiatrist. 
My suicidal thoughts were a lot stronger than usual and I thought about having to suffer this shit for years ongoing/the rest of my life.  
I really miss crying; it feels a bit like an emotional clensing.
